titleEn: Two Hands for a Duckling, Gently!

pages.text: "Wow, a duckling!" A tiny duckling peeped and walked through the doorway. Mr. Ming, who kept ducks in the lowest paddy, opened the duck house wide. Dingding wanted to hold the duckling.
Dingding grabbed it with one hand. "My hand is so strong!" The duckling's wings were pressed tightly inside the hand. It peeped urgently again and again.
Startled, Dingding opened their hand. The duckling dropped onto the straw and waddled away. "Oh... did that hurt?" Dingding hid their hands behind their back.
Mr. Ming crouched beside Dingding. "Ducklings are very delicate. Grabbing with one hand hurts them. Scoop them up with two hands." He cupped his hands together.
His hands made a little bowl. Dingding cupped both hands, too. "Like this?" "That's right. Two Hands for a Duckling, Gently!"
Dingding knelt on the straw floor and looked all around. There was a stone the duckling might trip over. Dingding picked it up and put it outside the duck house.

This time, Dingding made a bowl with both hands and gently scooped up the duckling. It curled into a little ball on their palms. "Two Hands for a Duckling, Gently!" Even Dingding's breathing was gentle.
Grandma came to the duck house. "Your hands have become a bowl." Dingding sniffed the warm straw smell on their palms. "It cried when I grabbed hard, but it stays still when I lift gently!"

Now Dingding had duckling rules. "One, make a bowl with both hands! Two, be very gentle! Three, clear away stones underfoot first!" Dingding set the duckling softly on the straw and stepped back. "Go slowly. I won't grab you."

Grandma stroked Dingding's back and hugged their shoulders. Small, delicate creatures needed two supporting hands to keep them from hurting. Dingding cupped their hands. "Two Hands for a Duckling, Gently!"
